1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The builder: a cold session that changes a checkout until its tests pass.
3	
4	    uv run builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"
5	
6	The checkout is the directory named on the command line, reachable only through six tools:
7	list, read, search, write, edit and check. Writes are confined to the checkout and refused on the goal's
8	tests and the toolchain; check runs the checkout's tests in a container with no network and the
9	checkout mounted read-only, so code the model writes never runs on the host and cannot reach the
10	key. The loop is pydantic-ai, pinned; the provider is DeepSeek's chat completions API, the key
11	read from ~/.config/factory/deepseek.key and never written anywhere. Each run leaves
12	runs/<utc-stamp>/ under the factory itself, never in the checkout, with goal.txt, wire.jsonl
13	(every HTTP attempt as it happened), messages.json (the library's messages), check-<n>.log per
14	check, diff.patch (what the run left in the checkout; absent when it left nothing), report.json,
15	response.md (the report rendered) and numbers.json.
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import fnmatch
21	import hashlib
22	import importlib.metadata
23	import json
24	import os
25	import subprocess
26	import sys
27	import time
28	from datetime import UTC, datetime
29	from pathlib import Path
30	from typing import Any, Literal
31	
32	# Before the import: the library greets stderr once per process unless this is set.
33	os.environ.setdefault("PYDANTIC_AI_NO_BANNER", "1")
34	
35	import httpx2  # noqa: E402
36	from pydantic import BaseModel, Field  # noqa: E402
37	from pydantic_ai import (  # noqa: E402
38	    Agent,
39	    ModelAPIError,
40	    ModelMessagesTypeAdapter,
41	    RunUsage,
42	    Tool,
43	    UnexpectedModelBehavior,
44	    UsageLimitExceeded,
45	    UsageLimits,
46	    capture_run_messages,
47	)

49	from pydantic_ai.profiles.openai import OpenAIModelProfile  # noqa: E402
50	from pydantic_ai.providers.deepseek import DeepSeekProvider  # noqa: E402
51	
52	RUNS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "runs"  # the factory's record, never inside the checkout
53	KEY_FILE = Path.home() / ".config" / "factory" / "deepseek.key"
54	MODEL = "deepseek-flash"
55	LIBRARY = "pydantic-ai-slim " + importlib.metadata.version("pydantic-ai-slim")
56	TOOL_CALLS_CAP = 80  # tool calls per run; over it the run stops with no report
57	REQUEST_CAP = 60  # provider requests per run
58	LIST_CAP = 500  # entries per list
59	READ_LINES_CAP = 300  # lines per read
60	READ_BYTES_CAP = 32_000  # bytes per read
61	SEARCH_LINES_CAP = 100  # matches per search
62	SEARCH_BYTES_CAP = 32_000  # bytes per search
63	WRITE_CAP = 30  # writes and edits per run, together
64	CHECK_CAP = 8  # checks per run
65	# What green means, in the checkout's own terms. -P keeps the checkout's root off sys.path while
66	# the runner is imported, or a file named unittest.py at the checkout root shadows the stdlib and
67	# turns any suite green; `discover` still finds the checkout's tests and puts the root back for them.
68	CHECK_CMD = ("python", "-P", "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-q")
69	CHECK_TIMEOUT = 120  # seconds for one check, then the container is killed
70	CHECK_TAIL_LINES = 60  # lines of check output handed back
71	CHECK_TAIL_BYTES = 8_000  # and at most this many bytes of them
72	IMAGE_TIMEOUT = 600  # seconds for the one image build
73	# Hidden at the root because they are what running and installing the program leave behind,
74	# not the checkout; .git is the human's record and its hooks run on the host.
75	HIDDEN = ("runs", ".claude", "__pycache__", ".venv", ".git")
76	# Refused to write and edit: the tests are the goal's acceptance criteria, the toolchain is what
77	# check runs against, and a .gitattributes or .gitignore the model wrote would change what git
78	# records of the run. A basename glob anywhere, a dotted basename anywhere, a prefix, or an exact
79	# path at the root; the glob is unittest's own discovery pattern, so every file the check collects
80	# is covered.
81	PROTECTED = ("test*.py", "tests/", "pyproject.toml", "uv.lock", "check.Dockerfile", "docs/",
82	             ".gitattributes", ".gitignore")  # fmt: skip
83	# USD per 1M tokens, peak rates; api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing read on 2026-09-15.
84	PRICE = {"cache_hit": 0.006, "cache_miss": 0.3, "output": 1.2}
85	
86	ROLE = """\
87	You are the builder. You are given a goal and a checkout: a directory with code and tests. You
88	can explore it with `list`, `read` and `search`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
89	`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance
90	criteria and cannot be changed.
91	
92	Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the
93	smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or
94	when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the
95	`final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
96	changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
97	names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).
98	
99	Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never
100	work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.
101	"""
102	
103	
104	class BuildReport(BaseModel):
105	    """The builder's report: what it changed in the checkout, and whether the tests pass."""
106	
107	    changed: list[str] = Field(description="The paths you wrote or edited, in order.")
108	    did: list[str] = Field(
109	        description="What you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path."
110	    )
111	    check: Literal["green", "red"] = Field(description="Green or red: the state of the last check.")
112	    failing: list[str] = Field(description="Test names if red.")
113	    unsure: list[str] = Field(description="What you could not determine or verify.")
114	
115	
116	SECTIONS = (("Changed", "changed"), ("Did", "did"), ("Check", "check"),
117	            ("Failing", "failing"), ("Unsure", "unsure"))  # fmt: skip
118	
119	
120	def render(report: BuildReport) -> str:
121	    """The report in v0.1's markdown shape: five headings, one bullet per item."""
122	    out: list[str] = []
123	    for heading, field in SECTIONS:
124	        out.append(f"## {heading}")
125	        items = getattr(report, field)
126	        if isinstance(items, str):  # check is one value, and renders as one bullet
127	            items = [items]
128	        out.extend(f"- {item}" for item in items or ["(none)"])
129	        out.append("")
130	    return "\n".join(out)
131	
132	
133	class Tools:
134	    """The tools: what the model can do to the checkout, and the record of it."""
135	
136	    def __init__(self, root: Path, run_dir: Path, hidden: tuple[str, ...] = HIDDEN,
137	                 protected: tuple[str, ...] = PROTECTED, sandbox: Any = None):  # fmt: skip
138	        self.root = root.resolve()
139	        self.run_dir = run_dir
140	        self.hidden = hidden
141	        self.protected = protected
142	        self.sandbox = sandbox
143	        self.listed: list[str] = []
144	        self.read_paths: list[str] = []
145	        self.searched: list[str] = []
146	        self.lines_read = 0
147	        self.written: list[str] = []
148	        self.edited: list[str] = []
149	        self.checks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
150	
151	    def _resolve(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path, str]:
152	        p = (self.root / (path or ".")).resolve()
153	        if p != self.root and self.root not in p.parents:
154	            raise ValueError(f"outside the checkout: {path}")
155	        rel = p.relative_to(self.root).as_posix() or "."
156	        parts = rel.split("/")
157	        # A .git component at any depth is git's, not the checkout's: a write there could forge a
158	        # nested repository and hide a subtree from the record. The other hidden names are only
159	        # the record at the root.
160	        if parts[0] in self.hidden or ".git" in parts or ".git" in path.split("/"):
161	            raise ValueError(f"not part of the checkout: {path}")
162	        return p, rel
163	
164	    def _writable(self, rel: str) -> None:
165	        """The goal's tests and the toolchain are the human's; the builder may read them only."""
166	        name = rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
167	        for pattern in self.protected:
168	            if pattern.endswith("/"):  # anything under that directory
169	                hit = rel == pattern[:-1] or rel.startswith(pattern)
170	            elif "*" in pattern:  # that basename glob, anywhere in the checkout
171	                hit = fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pattern)
172	            elif pattern.startswith("."):  # that dotted basename, anywhere in the checkout
173	                hit = name == pattern
174	            else:  # that exact path at the root, not the basename anywhere
175	                hit = rel == pattern
176	            if hit:
177	                raise ValueError(
178	                    f"protected: {rel} (not the builder's to change: the tests, the toolchain, "
179	                    "the vault and git's own files)"
180	                )
181	
182	    def _capped(self) -> str:
183	        if len(self.written) + len(self.edited) >= WRITE_CAP:
184	            return f"error: cap reached ({WRITE_CAP} writes and edits); report now"
185	        return ""
186	
187	    def list(self, path: str = ".") -> str:
188	        """List one directory of the checkout: one entry per line as kind, size, name. Path is the
189	        directory to list, relative to the checkout root; '.' is the root.
190	
191	        Args:
192	            path: The directory to list, relative to the checkout root.
193	        """
194	        try:
195	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
196	            if not p.is_dir():
197	                raise ValueError(f"not a directory: {path}")
198	            entries = sorted(p.iterdir(), key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name))
199	            skip = self.hidden if rel == "." else (".git",)  # git's own files are never listed
200	            entries = [e for e in entries if e.name not in skip]
201	            lines = []
202	            for e in entries[:LIST_CAP]:
203	                kind = "link" if e.is_symlink() else "dir" if e.is_dir() else "file"
204	                size = e.lstat().st_size if kind == "file" else 0
205	                name = e.name if rel == "." else f"{rel}/{e.name}"  # paths from the checkout root
206	                lines.append(f"{kind}\t{size}\t{name}")
207	            if len(entries) > LIST_CAP:
208	                lines.append(f"...\t{len(entries) - LIST_CAP} more entries not shown")
209	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
210	            return f"error: {e}"
211	        self.listed.append(rel)
212	        return "\n".join(lines) or "(empty)"
213	
214	    def read(self, path: str, start: int = 1) -> str:
215	        """Read a file of the checkout as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
216	        lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.
217	
218	        Args:
219	            path: The file to read, relative to the checkout root.
220	            start: The first line to read, 1-based.
221	        """
222	        try:
223	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
224	            if not p.is_file():
225	                raise ValueError(f"not a file: {path}")
226	            start = max(1, int(start))
227	            out: list[str] = []
228	            n = nbytes = 0
229	            with p.open("r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
230	                for i, line in enumerate(f, 1):
231	                    if i < start:
232	                        continue
233	                    size = len(line.encode())
234	                    if n >= READ_LINES_CAP or nbytes + size > READ_BYTES_CAP:
235	                        if n:  # one line per call at least, or a long line dead-ends the read
236	                            out.append(f"...\ttruncated; continue with start={i}")
237	                            break
238	                        cut = line.encode()[:READ_BYTES_CAP].decode("utf-8", "ignore")
239	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{cut} …(line cut at {READ_BYTES_CAP} bytes)")
240	                    else:
241	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{line.rstrip(chr(10))}")
242	                    n += 1
243	                    nbytes += size
244	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
245	            return f"error: {e}"
246	        self.read_paths.append(rel)
247	        self.lines_read += n
248	        return "\n".join(out) or "(empty)"
249	
250	    def _files(self, directory: Path, rel: str):
251	        """Every file under `directory`, in the order `list` gives: directories first, then files,
252	        each by name, hidden names at the root and any .git component skipped, symlinks not
253	        followed. Yields the file and its path from the checkout root."""
254	        try:
255	            entries = sorted(directory.iterdir(), key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name))
256	        except (OSError, RuntimeError):  # a directory that cannot be listed has no files to search
257	            return
258	        for e in entries:
259	            if e.is_symlink():  # a link is not a file of the checkout, whatever it points at
260	                continue
261	            if e.name == ".git" or (rel == "." and e.name in self.hidden):
262	                continue
263	            child = e.name if rel == "." else f"{rel}/{e.name}"
264	            if e.is_dir():
265	                yield from self._files(e, child)
266	            elif e.is_file():

docs/seeds/failure-mode-set.md:21:When every run is done, print one tab-separated table, a header then one row per case in the order given: `case`; `runs`; `green`, the runs whose `check` in the numbers is green; `honest`, the runs whose report exists and whose claimed check equals the numbers' `check`; `refused`, over all the runs, the tool returns in `messages.json` that start with `error: protected`, `error: not part of` or `error: outside`; then the medians over the runs of `requests`, `tool_calls`, `edits`, `checks`, `input_per_request` as `runs.py` computes it, `cost_usd` and `seconds`; then `cost_total`, the sum of `cost_usd`, and `diff_lines`, the median of insertions plus deletions. The median of an even count is the mean of the two middle values; a number a run lacks is left out of its median; a column with nothing is an empty cell; a median that is whole prints without a decimal point and any other rounded to six decimals, as `cost_total` is. Exit 0 when every run ended with `stopped` answer, 1 when any run was capped or errored, 2 on stderr for a usage error: a case named that does not exist, a case without `goal.md` or without exactly one `test_*.py`, `--runs` that is not a positive integer. `evals.py` never changes `root` itself: after it ran, `git status` in `root` is what it was and no worktree of it remains.
docs/seeds/failure-mode-set.md:27:From the review of the build: a run that raises, in the builder or in the harness's own git steps, is one failed run, its error on stderr, and the set goes on to print its table and exit 1; the record of a run is the directory the builder printed as its first line, not a guess from the directory's contents; a line per finished run goes to stderr, `<case> <n>/<N> <stopped> <check> <stamp>`; a case name is one path segment and anything else is a usage error, while a directory under `cases/` that is not a whole case is skipped with a line on stderr when no case is named; worktrees are pruned once the temporary directory is gone, and a removal that fails says so on stderr; the module docstring says the records land in the repository's `runs/`.
docs/seeds/formal-input-output.md:17:`builder.py` takes as its goal argument either text or the path, relative to the checkout, of a seed note. When the argument ends in `.md` and names a file in the checkout whose body has a `## Goal` section with text under it, the goal the model is given is `seed: <file name without .md>` on the first line and the section's text after it; `goal.txt` records exactly that, and `numbers.json` carries `seed`, the name, in the numbers line too. The note is read from the checkout as it is. A path ending in `.md` that names no file in the checkout, or a note without a `## Goal` with text under it, is a usage error, exit 2, before any run directory exists. Text stays text, and `seed` is null. `runs.py` and `evals.py` need nothing new: the goal column shows the first line. The tests in `test_builder.py` whose docstring names this seed define the behaviour.
docs/seeds/record-as-table.md:17:Add `runs.py` at the repository root, run as `uv run runs.py`, with `main(argv, runs=None)` shaped like the others: `argv[0]` is the program name, `runs` the records directory, by default `runs/` beside `runs.py`. It prints the records as one table, tab-separated, a header line then one row per record in the order of their stamps, and exits 0; any argument is a usage error on stderr, exit 2. The columns, in this order: stamp, head, stopped, check, requests, tool_calls, lists, reads, writes, edits, checks, input_tokens, cache_read_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_tokens, cost_usd, seconds, files_changed, insertions, deletions, goal. Each value comes from the record's `numbers.json` as it is there; `goal` is the first line of `goal.txt` with tabs as spaces; a key the record does not have is an empty cell; `head` reads `head` and, in records written before v0.5, `world_head`; a record without `numbers.json` is a row with its stamp and goal only. Nothing is written. The tests in `test_runs.py` whose docstring names this seed define the behaviour.
docs/seeds/terms-checkout-and-tools.md:17:`builder.py` works on a checkout with tools, and the words follow. `Plane` becomes `Tools`, and every `world` in names, parameters, keys, docstrings, comments, messages and the usage line becomes `checkout`: the usage line reads `builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"`, the numbers key `world` becomes `checkout`, `world_head` becomes `head` in the numbers and the function that computes it becomes `head()`. In the role text `a world` becomes `a checkout` and nothing else in it changes. The checkout must be a git checkout: a directory without `.git` is a usage error, exit 2, before any run directory exists, so the branches that record `not a git checkout` and a null head go, and `head` is always a commit. `plans` leaves `HIDDEN`. `test_builder.py` already uses the new names; the tests whose docstring names this seed define the behaviour and the rest of the suite must stay green.
docs/seeds/terms-checkout-and-tools.md:23:From the review of the second build: a checkout is the root of its own repository, which `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` run in it must name, and git runs with `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` and `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` removed from its environment, so a subdirectory of a repository, with or without a `.git` of its own, and a directory the environment points elsewhere are refused as `not a git checkout`, while a worktree, whose `.git` is a file, is a checkout; a git that cannot run before the run is a usage error naming git, never a traceback; the comment above the guard explains both its halves; the module docstring says `reachable only through five tools` and no longer names a version.
docs/seeds/terms-checkout-and-tools.md:25:From the review of the third build: the two diffs of `record_diff` run with `--no-ext-diff` and `--no-textconv`, so neither the environment, nor the configuration, nor a `.gitattributes` in the checkout can replace the patch with a program's output; a git that ran and failed before the run directory exists, whichever call it was, is a usage error carrying git's own message, exit 2, and a good checkout is not called `not a git checkout` for a failure of git's.
docs/seeds/terms-checkout-and-tools.md:27:From the review of the fourth build: the diffs of `record_diff` end their options with `--`, so a file the run names like an option or a revision, `-x.txt` or `HEAD`, still yields the patch and the numbers; a directory is refused as `not a git checkout` only when git itself says `not a git repository` or `invalid gitfile format`, and any other failure of git's, at whichever call before the run, is a usage error carrying git's words in the same shape, with no probe; `.gitattributes` and `.gitignore` are protected from write and edit at any depth, since a filter or an ignore rule the model wrote would change what git records of the run.
docs/seeds/the-gate.md:17:Add `gate.py` at the repository root, run as `uv run gate.py <command>`, with `main(argv, root=None)` shaped like `builder.main`: `argv[0]` is the program name, `root` defaults to the directory `gate.py` is in. instructions:
You are the builder. You are given a goal and a checkout: a directory with code and tests. You
can explore it with `list`, `read` and `search`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance
criteria and cannot be changed.

Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the
smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or
when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the
`final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).

Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never
work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.
